(* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)
LZp := -1/4 FS[Zp, mu, nu] FS[Zp, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZp^2 Zp[mu] Zp[mu];

LVq := -1/2 FS[Vqbar, mu, nu] FS[Vq, mu, nu] + MVq^2 Vqbar[mu] Vq[mu];

LYq := -1/2 FS[Yqbar, mu, nu] FS[Yq, mu, nu] + MYq^2 Yqbar[mu] Yq[mu];

(* ----- Free-field terms: real scalars ----- *)
LH2 := 1/2 del[H2, mu] del[H2, mu] - 1/2 MH2^2 H2^2;

LH3 := 1/2 del[H3, mu] del[H3, mu] - 1/2 MH3^2 H3^2;

LH0 := 1/2 del[H0, mu] del[H0, mu] - 1/2 MH0^2 H0^2;

(* ----- Free-field terms: complex scalars ----- *)
LHP := DC[HPbar, mu] DC[HP, mu] - MHP^2 HPbar HP;

LHV := DC[HVbar, mu] DC[HV, mu] - MHV^2 HVbar HV;

LHY := DC[HYbar, mu] DC[HY, mu] - MHY^2 HYbar HY;

(* ----- Free-field terms: Dirac fermions ----- *)
LDq := I Dqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Dq, mu] - MDq Dqbar.Dq;

LSq := I Sqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Sq, mu] - MSq Sqbar.Sq;

LTq := I Tqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Tq, mu] - MTq Tqbar.Tq;

LEl := Block[{sp, ff},
  ExpandIndices[I Elbar[sp, ff].Ga[mu].DC[El[sp, ff], mu] - MEl Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff]]
];

(* ----- New Yukawa interactions (mass eigenstates; paper Table scalar-fermion) ----- *)
LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, yuk},
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
    (* heavy quark diagonal scalars *)
    - (MDq/v3)*c13 Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]*HV
    - (MDq/v3)*s13 MDq/MDq Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]*HV
    + (MDq/v3) Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjP.Dq[sp, cc]*HV*0
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ];
  (* Explicit paper couplings, flavour-diagonal (Table scalar-fermion) *)
  ExpandIndices[
    (* H3 / H2 / H0 / h-like to heavy quarks: H3 chi-like *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* heavy leptons: H0, h, H2, H3 *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* charged scalar <-> fermion (paper coefficients) *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HC[HPbar[sp].El[sp, ff].vl[sp, ff]]
    - Sqrt[2]*s12*mup/v2 Dqbar... ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  (* rebuilt cleanly below *)
];

LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
    (* D,S,T with neutral scalars (chi- and eta/rho-like) *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* heavy leptons with neutral scalars *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* H^{+-} with d-type quarks: H^- \bar D d etc. *)
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MDq/v3) HC[HPbar].Dq.dq*CKM[ff1, ff2]
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13/v1) HC[HPbar].dq.Dq*dqmass
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ];
  yuk = 0;
  (* Rebuild without accidental incomplete terms *)
  ExpandIndices[
    (* neutral H3 (chi-like) Yukawas *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* H2 *)
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    (* H (SM-like component) *)
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    (* H0 CP-odd *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    (* HV = H^{+-Q_V}: HV^- \bar D d, HV^- \bar t T  (paper) *)
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MDq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.Dq.dq
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13*MDq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.dq.Dq
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MTq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.Tq.tq
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13*MTq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.tq.Tq
    (* HY = H^{+-Q_Y}: HY^+ \bar u D, HY^+ \bar T b  (paper) *)
    + Sqrt[2]*(c23*MDq/v3) HYbar.ProjM.uq.Dq
    + Sqrt[2]*(s23*ymup/vev) HYbar.ProjM.Dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*(c23*MTq/v3) HYbar.ProjM.Tq.bq
    + Sqrt[2]*(s23*ymb/vev) HYbar.ProjM.bq.Tq
    (* HP couples SM charged fermions / heavy leptons *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c12*ymup/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.uq.dq
    + Sqrt[2]*s12*ymb/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*c12*yme/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.e.ll
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  + HC[
    Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HPbar.El.vl
    - Sqrt[2]*c23*MEl/v3 HVbar.El.l
    - Sqrt[2]*s12*MMU/vev HVbar... ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
];

(* Final clean Yukawa term *)
LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, ff, cc},
  ExpandIndices[
    (* neutral scalars with heavy quarks D,S,T *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* neutral scalars with heavy leptons *)
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    (* HV: H^{-Q_V} bar{D} d and bar{t} T (paper Eq. scalar-fermion) *)
    - Sqrt[2]*c13*MDq/v3 Conjugate[HVbar].Dq.dq
    - Sqrt[2]*s13*ymb/vev Conjugate[HVbar].dq.Dq
    - Sqrt[2]*c13*MTq/v3 Conjugate[HVbar].Tq.tq
    - Sqrt[2]*s13*ymt/vev Conjugate[HVbar].tq.Tq
    (* HY: H^{+Q_Y} bar{u} D and bar{T} b *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c23*MDq/v3 HYbar.uq.Dq
    + Sqrt[2]*s23*ymup/vev HYbar.Dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*c23*MTq/v3 HYbar.Tq.bq
    + Sqrt[2]*s23*ymb/vev HYbar.bq.Tq
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  + HC[
    ExpandIndices[
      Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HPbar.El.vl
      - Sqrt[2]*c23*MEl/v3 HVbar.El.l
      + Sqrt[2]*s12*ymup/vev HPbar.uq.dq
      - Sqrt[2]*c12*ymb/vev HPbar.dq.uq
      + Sqrt[2]*s23*yme/vev HYbar.El.l
      - Sqrt[2]*c12*MMU/vev HPbar... ,
      FlavorExpand -> SU2D
    ]
  ]
];

778:     ,

786:     - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
787:     - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
788:     - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
789:     - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
790:     - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
791:     - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
792:     - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H

795:     + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
796:     + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
797:     + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
798:     (* charged scalar <-> fermion (paper coefficients) *)
799:     + Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HC[HPbar[sp].El[sp, ff].vl[sp, ff]]
800:     - Sqrt[2]*s12*mup/v2 Dqbar... ,
801:     FlavorExpand -> SU2D
802:   ]

804: ];

808:     (* D,S,T with neutral scalars (chi- and eta/rho-like) *)

810:     - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
811:     - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
812:     - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
813:     - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
814:     - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
815:     - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
816:     - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H

819:     - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
820:     + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
821:     + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
822:     + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3

825:     - Sqrt[2]*(s13/v1) HC[HPbar].dq.Dq*dqmass
826:     ,

828:   ];

831:   ExpandIndices[
832:     (* neutral H3 (chi-like) Yukawas *)

834:     - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
835:     - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3

839:     - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2

845:     - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H

(* *****   Lagrangian   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

(* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)
LZp := -1/4 FS[Zp, mu, nu] FS[Zp, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZp^2 Zp[mu] Zp[mu];

LVq := -1/2 FS[Vqbar, mu, nu] FS[Vq, mu, nu] + MVq^2 Vqbar[mu] Vq[mu];

LYq := -1/2 FS[Yqbar, mu, nu] FS[Yq, mu, nu] + MYq^2 Yqbar[mu] Yq[mu];

(* ----- Free-field terms: real scalars ----- *)
LH2 := 1/2 del[H2, mu] del[H2, mu] - 1/2 MH2^2 H2^2;

LH3 := 1/2 del[H3, mu] del[H3, mu] - 1/2 MH3^2 H3^2;

LH0 := 1/2 del[H0, mu] del[H0, mu] - 1/2 MH0^2 H0^2;

(* ----- Free-field terms: complex scalars ----- *)
LHP := DC[HPbar, mu] DC[HP, mu] - MHP^2 HPbar HP;

LHV := DC[HVbar, mu] DC[HV, mu] - MHV^2 HVbar HV;

LHY := DC[HYbar, mu] DC[HY, mu] - MHY^2 HYbar HY;

(* ----- Free-field terms: Dirac fermions ----- *)
LDq := I Dqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Dq, mu] - MDq Dqbar.Dq;

LSq := I Sqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Sq, mu] - MSq Sqbar.Sq;

LTq := I Tqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Tq, mu] - MTq Tqbar.Tq;

LEl := Block[{sp, ff},
  ExpandIndices[I Elbar[sp, ff].Ga[mu].DC[El[sp, ff], mu] - MEl Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff]]
];

(* ----- New Yukawa interactions (mass eigenstates; paper Table scalar-fermion) ----- *)
LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, yuk},
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
    (* heavy quark diagonal scalars *)
    - (MDq/v3)*c13 Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]*HV
    - (MDq/v3)*s13 MDq/MDq Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]*HV
    + (MDq/v3) Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjP.Dq[sp, cc]*HV*0
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ];
  (* Explicit paper couplings, flavour-diagonal (Table scalar-fermion) *)
  ExpandIndices[
    (* H3 / H2 / H0 / h-like to heavy quarks: H3 chi-like *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* heavy leptons: H0, h, H2, H3 *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* charged scalar <-> fermion (paper coefficients) *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HC[HPbar[sp].El[sp, ff].vl[sp, ff]]
    - Sqrt[2]*s12*mup/v2 Dqbar... ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  (* rebuilt cleanly below *)
];

LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
    (* D,S,T with neutral scalars (chi- and eta/rho-like) *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* heavy leptons with neutral scalars *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* H^{+-} with d-type quarks: H^- \bar D d etc. *)
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MDq/v3) HC[HPbar].Dq.dq*CKM[ff1, ff2]
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13/v1) HC[HPbar].dq.Dq*dqmass
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ];
  yuk = 0;
  (* Rebuild without accidental incomplete terms *)
  ExpandIndices[
    (* neutral H3 (chi-like) Yukawas *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* H2 *)
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    (* H (SM-like component) *)
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    (* H0 CP-odd *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    (* HV = H^{+-Q_V}: HV^- \bar D d, HV^- \bar t T  (paper) *)
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MDq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.Dq.dq
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13*MDq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.dq.Dq
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MTq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.Tq.tq
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13*MTq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.tq.Tq
    (* HY = H^{+-Q_Y}: HY^+ \bar u D, HY^+ \bar T b  (paper) *)
    + Sqrt[2]*(c23*MDq/v3) HYbar.ProjM.uq.Dq
    + Sqrt[2]*(s23*ymup/vev) HYbar.ProjM.Dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*(c23*MTq/v3) HYbar.ProjM.Tq.bq
    + Sqrt[2]*(s23*ymb/vev) HYbar.ProjM.bq.Tq
    (* HP couples SM charged fermions / heavy leptons *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c12*ymup/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.uq.dq
    + Sqrt[2]*s12*ymb/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*c12*yme/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.e.ll
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  + HC[
    Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HPbar.El.vl
    - Sqrt[2]*c23*MEl/v3 HVbar.El.l
    - Sqrt[2]*s12*MMU/vev HVbar... ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
];

(* Final clean Yukawa term *)

  ExpandIndices[
    (* neutral scalars with heavy quarks D,S,T *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* neutral scalars with heavy leptons *)
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0

    - Sqrt[2]*c13*MTq/v3 Conjugate[HVbar].Tq.tq
    - Sqrt[2]*s13*ymt/vev Conjugate[HVbar].tq.Tq

    + Sqrt[2]*c23*MDq/v3 HYbar.uq.Dq
    + Sqrt[2]*s23*ymup/vev HYbar.Dq.uq

\subsection{Gauge Boson Self-couplings}
The gauge boson self-couplings are given here, with all momenta out-going. The three-point and four point couplings take the following form
\begin{eqnarray}
V_1^\mu(k_1) V_2^\nu(k_2) V_3^\rho(k_3)&&g_{V_1V_2V_3}\left[\left(k_1-k_2\right)^{\rho } \eta _{\mu ,\nu }+\left(k_2-k_3\right)^{\mu } \eta _{\nu ,\rho }+\left(k_3-k_1\right)^{\nu } \eta _{\mu ,\rho }\right], \nn\\
V_1^\mu V_2^\nu V_3^\rho V_4^\sigma &&g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^1(\eta _{\mu ,\sigma } \eta _{\nu ,\rho }+\eta _{\mu ,\rho } \eta _{\nu ,\sigma }-2 \eta _{\mu ,\nu } \eta _{\rho ,\sigma }),  \nonumber \\
V_1^\mu V_2^\nu V_3^\rho V_4^\sigma &&g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^2[\left(3-\left(a_+ +2\right)s_W^2\right)\eta _{\mu ,\sigma } \eta _{\nu ,\rho } +2 \left(a_- +1\right)  s_W^2 \eta _{\mu ,\rho } \eta _{\nu ,\sigma } \nn \\
&&-\left(3+\left(a_- -2\right)s_W^2\right)\eta _{\mu ,\nu } \eta _{\rho ,\sigma}],  \nonumber \\
V_1^\mu V_2^\nu V_3^\rho V_4^\sigma &&g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^3[\left(\sqrt{3} \beta -3\right) \eta _{\mu ,\sigma } \eta _{\nu ,\rho }-2 \sqrt{3} \beta  \eta _{\mu ,\rho } \eta _{\nu ,\sigma } \nn \\
&&+\left(\sqrt{3} \beta +3\right) \eta _{\mu ,\nu } \eta _{\rho ,\sigma}].
\end{eqnarray}

615: \subsection{Yukawa Sector}
616: The Lagrangian of the Yukawa sector is
617: \be
618: \cL_{Yuk}=\cL^{q}_{Yuk}+\cL^{l}_{Yuk},
619: \ee
620: where $\cL^{q}_{Yuk}$ and $\cL^{l}_{Yuk}$ are the Lagrangians for quarks and leptons as follows:
621: \bea
622: -\cL^{q}_{Yuk}&=&y^u_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\eta u_{jR}+y^u_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\rho^* u_{jR} + y^d_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\rho d_{jR}+y^d_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\eta^* d_{jR} \nn \\
623:              &+&y^J_{ik}\bar q_{iL}\chi J_{kR}+y^J_{33}\bar q_{3L}\chi^* J_{3R}+h.c., \\
624: -\cL^{l}_{Yuk}&=&y^e_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\eta^* e_{nR}+y^E_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\chi^* E_{nR}+h.c..
625: \eea
626: Here, the $i$ ($k$) index runs from 1 to 2 while the $j$ ($m$, $n$) runs from 1 to 3, respectively. The $J_{kR}$ refers to the right-handed heavy quarks $D$ and $S$ while the $J_{3R}$ denotes the right-handed quark $T$. Also, the $E_{nR}$ represents the right-handed heavy leptons $E_e$, $E_\mu$ and $E_\tau$. All the fermions become massive after spontaneously symmetry breaking.

634: \end{array}\right)^\prime_L=U^{-1}_L
635: \left(\begin{array}{c}

637: c \\
638: t \\
639: \end{array}\right)_L, \quad
640: \left(\begin{array}{c}

\subsection{Yukawa Sector}
The Lagrangian of the Yukawa sector is
\be
\cL_{Yuk}=\cL^{q}_{Yuk}+\cL^{l}_{Yuk},
\ee
where $\cL^{q}_{Yuk}$ and $\cL^{l}_{Yuk}$ are the Lagrangians for quarks and leptons as follows:
\bea
-\cL^{q}_{Yuk}&=&y^u_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\eta u_{jR}+y^u_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\rho^* u_{jR} + y^d_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\rho d_{jR}+y^d_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\eta^* d_{jR} \nn \\
             &+&y^J_{ik}\bar q_{iL}\chi J_{kR}+y^J_{33}\bar q_{3L}\chi^* J_{3R}+h.c., \\
-\cL^{l}_{Yuk}&=&y^e_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\eta^* e_{nR}+y^E_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\chi^* E_{nR}+h.c..
\eea
Here, the $i$ ($k$) index runs from 1 to 2 while the $j$ ($m$, $n$) runs from 1 to 3, respectively. The $J_{kR}$ refers to the right-handed heavy quarks $D$ and $S$ while the $J_{3R}$ denotes the right-handed quark $T$. Also, the $E_{nR}$ represents the right-handed heavy leptons $E_e$, $E_\mu$ and $E_\tau$. All the fermions become massive after spontaneously symmetry breaking. 

The mass eigenstates (labelled with the superscript $\prime$) can be related with the weak eigenstates by unitary matrices
\be
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=U^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)_L, \quad
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=V^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)_L,
\ee
from which one can define the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) matrix as
\be
V_{\rm CKM}=U_L^\dag V_L.
\ee
We only introduce the rotation matrix of the left-handed quarks in the SM. The rotation matrices of the right-handed fermions can be absorbed by fermion fields redefinition due to their features of the gauge-singlet and the universality of the fermion-gauge couplings. The lack of the right-handed neutrinos makes it possible for the left-handed neutrinos to have the same rotation matrix as the left-handed electron (muon, tau), which leads to the similar CKM matrix equals to the Identity matrix. Besides, we have made an assumption that the third member of every fermion triplet or anti-triplet is already in its mass eigenstate~\cite{Buras:2012dp} such that we no longer need introduce their rotation matrix.

It is worth mentioning that the unitary matrices $U_L$ and the $V_L$ each individual have the physics meaning in the 331 model. That is owing to the non-universality couplings of the left-handed quarks with the $Z^\prime$ boson, originating from the different representations among the three SM left-handed quark flavors. 


\subsection{Electric Charge and Mass Spectrum in the 331 model}
In this section, we summarize the electric charge and mass spectrum of the new particles in the 331 model.
The electric charges of the new gauge bosons $Y$ and $V$ are $\pm (\sqrt{3}\beta+1)/2$ and $\pm (\sqrt{3}\beta-1)/2$ respectively. If we assume that
they are integers, $\beta$ will be restricted to some specific numbers which are
\be
\beta=\pm \frac{n}{\sqrt{3}},~~n=1,3,5,\cdots.
\ee
To ensure $M_{Z^\prime}^2\approx(c_W g v_3)^2/[3(1-(1+\beta^2)s_W^2)]$ being positive definite, $\beta$ must satisfy
\be
\beta^2<\frac{1-s_W^2}{s_W^2},
\ee
which further fix $n=1$ or 3, leading to $\beta=\pm \sqrt{3}$, $\pm 1/\sqrt{3}$. Table~\ref{tbl:charge} shows the electric charges of the new particles in the 331 model for those four different choices of $\beta$.

The Lagrangian of the gauge sector is
\be
\cL_{Gauge}=-\frac{1}{4}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}-\frac{1}{4}B_{\mu\nu}B^{\mu\nu},
\ee
where $F_{\mu\nu}$ and $B_{\mu\nu}$ are field strength tensors of $SU(3)_L$ and $U(1)_X$
\be
F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu W^i_\nu-\partial_\nu W^i_\mu, \label{2} \quad
B_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu X_\nu-\partial_\nu X_\mu.
\ee
Here, $W^i_\mu$ and $X_\mu$ denotes the gauge fields of $SU(3)_L$ and $U(1)_X$, respectively, where the index $i$ runs from 1 to 8.


After the spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB), gauge bosons obtain their masses from the kinetic terms of the Higgs fields
\be
\cL_{Higgs}^{kinetic}=(D_\mu \rho)^\dagger (D^\mu \rho)+(D_\mu \eta)^\dagger (D^\mu \eta)+(D_\mu \chi)^\dagger (D^\mu \chi). \label{0}
\ee
We explicitly write out the specific terms responsible for the masses of the gauge bosons
\bea
\cL_{Gauge}^{mass}&=&\left<\chi\right>^\dag G_\mu^\dag G^\mu \left<\chi\right>+ \left<\rho\right>^\dag G_\mu^\dag G^\mu \left<\rho\right>+ \left<\eta\right>^\dag G_\mu^\dag G^\mu \left<\eta\right> \notag\\
   &=&(\left<\chi\right>+ \left<\rho\right>+ \left<\eta\right>)^\dag G_\mu^\dag G^\mu(\left<\chi\right>+ \left<\rho\right>+ \left<\eta\right>) \notag\\
   &=&\frac{1}{2}\left(
                  \begin{array}{ccc}
                    v_2 & v_1 & v_3 \\
                  \end{array}
                \right)
     G_\mu^\dag G^\mu
     \left(
       \begin{array}{c}
         v_2 \\
         v_1 \\
         v_3 \\
       \end{array}
     \right)\label{gaugemass},
\eea
where 
\bea
&G_\mu&=gW^i_\mu T^i + g_X X X_\mu T^9  \label{Gmu} \nn \\ 
&=& {1 \over 2} \left(
\begin{array}{ccc}
g(W_\mu^3+{1 \over \sqrt{3}} W_\mu^8)+2g_X X X_\mu & \sqrt{2} gW_\mu^+ & \sqrt{2} gY_\mu^{+Q_Y}  \\ \nn
\sqrt{2} gW_\mu^-  & -g(W_\mu^3-{1 \over \sqrt{3}} W_\mu^8)+2g_X X_\mu & \sqrt{2} gV_\mu^{+Q_V}   \\ \nn
\sqrt{2} gY_\mu^{-Q_Y}  & \sqrt{2} gV_\mu^{-Q_V}  & -{2 \over \sqrt{3}} gW_\mu^8+2g_X X X_\mu
\end{array}\right). \\
\eea
In the above equation, $g$ and $g_X$ are coupling constants of $SU(3)_L$ and $U(1)_X$ respectively. $2T^i$ are eight Gell-Mann Matrices. $T^9$ is just the Identity matrix. $X$ is the $U(1)_X$ quantum number of some specific Higgs fields. We also define the mass eigenstates of the charged gauge bosons as follows 
\be
W^\pm_\mu=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(W^1_\mu \mp iW^2_\mu), \quad
Y^{\pm Q_Y}_\mu=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(W^4_\mu \mp iW^5_\mu), \quad

\ee

 \nn

  &+&~\frac{1}{8}v_2^2\left[gW_\mu^3+\frac{1}{\sqrt3}gW_\mu^8-(1+\frac{\beta}{\sqrt3})g_XX_\mu)\right]^2.
\eea

The mass spectrum of all the new particles introduced in the 331 model in the decoupling limit $v_3 \gg v_{1,2}$. The scalar masses are given by
\begin{itemize}
  \item Neutral Scalars
    \begin{align}
    &m_h^2 = \frac{2\left(\lambda_1 v_1^4+\lambda_{12}v_1^2 v_2^2+\lambda_2 v_2^4\right)}{v^2}, 
    && M_{H_2}^2 = \frac{v^2}{v_1 v_2}fv_3,\label{4}\\
    & M_{H_3}^2 = 2 \lambda _3 v_3^2,\label{5}
    && M^2_{H_0}= (\frac{v_1v_2}{v_3}+\frac{v_1v_3}{v_2}+\frac{v_2 v_3}{v_1})f.
    \end{align}
  \item Charged Scalars
    \bea
    M^2_{H^\pm}&=&\frac{2fv_3+\lambda^\prime_{12}v_1v_2}{2v_1v_2}v^2, \\
    M^2_{H^{\pm Q_Y}}&=&\frac{2fv_1+\lambda^\prime_{23}v_2 v_3}{2v_2 v_3}(v_2^2+v_3^2), \\
    M^2_{H^{\pm Q_V}}&=&\frac{2fv_2+\lambda^\prime_{13}v_1 v_3}{2v_1 v_3}(v_1^2+v_3^2).
    \eea
\end{itemize}
In the above neutral scalars, $h$, $H_2$ and $H_3$ are the CP-even eigenstates, while $H_0$ is the CP-odd eigenstate. Owing to the residue $SU(2)$ symmetry after the first step of spontaneously symmetry breaking at the high energy scale $v_3$, the masses of the $H^\pm$, $H_2$ and $H_0$  scalars are nearly degenerate, i.e.
\beq
M_{H^\pm}^2\approx M_{H_2}^2\approx M_{H_0}^2\approx \frac{fv_3}{v_1v_2}(v_1^2+v_2^2).
\eeq

The gauge boson masses are
\bea
&& M^2_Z= \frac{1}{4c_W^2}g^2v^2, \quad ~~
M^2_{Z^\prime} = \frac{c^2_W g^2 v_3^2}{3\left[1-(1+\beta^2)s^2_W\right]}, \label{3} \\
&& M^2_{W^\pm}=\frac{1}{4}g^2v^2, \qquad
M^2_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}= \frac{1}{4}g^2(v_3^2+v_2^2),\qquad
M^2_{V^{\pm Q_V}}=\frac{1}{4}g^2(v_3^2+v_1^2).
\eea
where $c_W\equiv \cos\theta_w$ and $s_W\equiv \sin\theta_w$. Note that $M_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}$ and $M_{V^{\pm Q_V}}$ are very close in the decoupling limit but not equal. The mass splitting should obey the following inequality
\be
\big|M^2_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}-M^2_{V^{\pm Q_V}}\big|<M_{W^\pm}^2,
\label{deltaM_VY}
\ee
which means that $\big|M_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}-M_{V^{\pm Q_V}}\big|$ is typically a few\gev.
The relation between the mass of $Z^\prime$ and the mass of $Y^{\pm Q_Y}$ or $V^{\pm Q_V}$ is
\be
M_{Z^\prime}^2=\frac{4c_W^2}{3\left[1-(1+\beta^2)s_W^2\right]}M_{Y(V)^{\pm Q_{Y(V)}}}^2+\cO (v_1^2).\label{zpvy}
\ee

As the heavy fermion masses arise from Yukawa interaction, there's no restriction on them. 

\newpage
\subsection{Residual $Z_2$ symmetry, dark matter and long-lived particles}

As pointed out in Ref.~\cite{Mizukoshi:2010ky}, after the SSB, there is a residual global symmetry $U(1)_G$ which ensures the lightest neutral particle to be dark matter~(DM) candidate. However, the lightest new particle could be charged for some $\beta$ values. Such a lightest charged particle is stable and not allowed by the well measured DM relic abundance. One can assume that  the lightest charged particle decays eventually through high dimensional operators induced by unknown interactions at a much higher energy scale. In many new physics models such a lightest charged particle are long-lived. We name it as a long-lived particle (LLP). Those long-lived charged particles have a very interesting collider signature in high energy collision~\cite{Aaboud:2016uth,ATLAS:2014fka,Chatrchyan:2013oca}. 

Here we introduce a simple ``$Z_2$" symmetry to help understanding the stability of the lightest particle of the charged gauge bosons $(W, V, Y)$. The charged gauge bosons correspond to the raising and lowering operators made by non-Cartan generators. Define the raising and lowering operators as
\beq
I_\pm=T_1\pm i T_2,\qquad V_\pm=T_4\pm i T_5,\qquad U_\pm=T_6\pm i T_7.
\eeq
The communication relations 
\beq
[I_+, V_-]=-U_-,~[I_+, U_+]=V_+,~[U_+, V_-]=T_-,
\eeq
and their hermitian conjugation tell us that the $W$ boson has to couple to a $V$ boson and a $Y$ boson. Hence, in the triple gauge boson interaction, one can assign $Z_2$-even quantum number to one gauge boson while $Z_2$-odd quantum number to the other two gauge bosons. For $W$, $Y$ and $V$ bosons, we take the following $Z_2$ quantum number assignment
\beq
Z_2\left(W\right)=+,\qquad Z_2\left(Y,~V\right)=-.\label{eq:odd1}
\eeq
We further require the gauge bosons associated with the Cartan generators exhibit the $Z_2$-even quantum number, i.e.
\beq
Z_2\left(\gamma,~Z_\mu,~Z^\prime_\mu\right)=+.
\eeq
In terms of the fermions, the upper two components in the fermion triplets are SM fermions ($f_{SM}$) which must be $Z_2$-even. Therefore, the lowest component, i.e. new heavy fermions, is $Z_2$-odd because another $Z_2$-odd gauge boson can connect the lowest component to one of the upper two components. As a result, we have the $Z_2$ assignment of fermions as follows
\be
Z_2\left(f_{SM}\right)=+,\qquad Z_2\left(E_\ell,~D,~S,~T\right)=-,\label{eq:odd2}
\ee
where $f_{SM}$ denote all the SM fermions. For the case of the scalars, the charged scalar whose electric charge is the same as the charged gauge boson will share the same $Z_2$ quantum number due to the Goldstone Equivalence Theorem. Therefore, we have
\be
Z_2\left(h,~H_2,~H_3,~H_0\right)=+,\qquad Z_2\left(H^{\pm Q_Y},~H^{\pm Q_V}\right)=-.\label{eq:odd3}
\ee
There are totally 14 $Z_2$-odd particles from \eqref{eq:odd1}, \eqref{eq:odd2} and \eqref{eq:odd3}.

Since the DM candidate is an electrically neutral particle in the $Z_2$-odd sector. There are only two choices of $\beta$ that can have such a neutral particle:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\beta=-1/\sqrt{3}$ ($Q_Y=0$): the DM candidate is $Y$ or $H^{Q_Y}$;
  \item $\beta=+1/\sqrt{3}$ ($Q_V=Q_E=0$): the DM candiate is $V$, $H^{Q_V}$ or $E_\ell$.
\end{itemize}
The detailed study on the dark matter is beyond the scope of the current paper, a recent review on this aspect can be found in~\cite{daSilva:2014qba}.

In the case of $\beta=\pm\sqrt{3}$, there will a charged LLP. In general there are many possibilities for LLP. But 
among them, the so-called $R$-hadron~\cite{Aad:2013gva} is more interesting. In this case, one of the three heavy quarks will be the lightest particle in the $Z_2$-odd sector. This heavy quark, say $D$ without any loss of generality, can pick up  another light quark, say $u$ quark, in the vacuum to form a hadronic bound state $D\bar{u}$. In Table~\ref{tbl:Rhadron}, we display all the possible $R$-hadron state with integer electric charge and only considering the first generation light quark component. The lightest $R$-hadron will be stable because there's no other thing it can decay into. For the sake of comparison, we also list the $R$-hadron state for $\beta=\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. Differently, they can decay to DM and another SM meson~(pion, Kaon, D-meson and B-meson).

548: The Lagrangian of the fermion section is 
549: \be
550: \cL_{\rm Fermion}=\bar\psi^\alpha i D_\mu \gamma^\mu \psi^\alpha,
551: \ee
552: where the superscript ``$\alpha$" denotes the fermion flavor. The covariant derivative is defined as follows
553: \be
554: D_\mu=\partial_\mu-igW^i_\mu T^i-ig_X X_\mu.
555: \ee
556: It is useful to write down the covariant derivatives acting on the fermion fields with different representations:
557: \begin{itemize}
558:   \item triplet $\psi_L$ $D_\mu \psi_L =\partial_\mu \psi_L - igW^i_\mu T^i \psi_L - ig_X X X_\mu \psi_L$;
559:   \item anti-triplet $\bar \psi_L$ $D_\mu \bar \psi_L =\partial_\mu \bar \psi_L + igW^i_\mu (T^i)^T \bar \psi_L - ig_X X X_\mu \bar \psi_L$;
560:   \item singlet $\psi_R$ $D_\mu \psi_R =\partial_\mu \psi_R - ig_X X X_\mu \psi_R$,
561: \end{itemize}
562: where $X$ is the fermions under $U(1)_X$. In this work the quark fields of the first and second genrations are required to be in the triplet representation of the $SU(3)_L$ group while the third generation quarks are in the anti-triplet representation. Therefore we can write the quark fields as follows:
563: \be
564: q_{1L}=\left(\begin{array}{c}
565: u  \\
566: d  \\
567: D  \\
568: \end{array}\right)_L, \quad
569: q_{2L}=\left(\begin{array}{c}
570: c  \\
571: s  \\
572: S  \\
573: \end{array}\right)_L, \quad
574: q_{3L}=\left(\begin{array}{c}
575: b  \\
576: -t \\
577: T  \\
578: \end{array}\right)_L .
579: \ee
580: Note that the $t$ and $b$ assignments are different from the SM as a result of requiring $q_{3L}$ being an anti-triplet. The extra minus sign in front of $t$ is to ensure generating the same Feynman vertices as those in the SM. The new heavy quarks are denoted as $D$, $S$ and $T$ with electric charges
581: \be
582: Q_D=Q_S=\frac{1}{6}-\frac {\sqrt{3}}{2}\beta, \quad\quad
583: Q_T=\frac{1}{6}+\frac {\sqrt{3}}{2}\beta.
584: \ee
585: All the lepton fields of the three generations are all treated as anti-triplets to guarantee the gauge anomaly cancellation, which requires equal numbers of triplets and anti-triplets. The lepton fields are given by
586: \be
587: l_{1L}=\left(\begin{array}{c}

739: (* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)
740: LZp := -1/4 FS[Zp, mu, nu] FS[Zp, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZp^2 Zp[mu] Zp[mu];

742: LVq := -1/2 FS[Vqbar, mu, nu] FS[Vq, mu, nu] + MVq^2 Vqbar[mu] Vq[mu];

744: LYq := -1/2 FS[Yqbar, mu, nu] FS[Yq, mu, nu] + MYq^2 Yqbar[mu] Yq[mu];

746: (* ----- Free-field terms: real scalars ----- *)
747: LH2 := 1/2 del[H2, mu] del[H2, mu] - 1/2 MH2^2 H2^2;

749: LH3 := 1/2 del[H3, mu] del[H3, mu] - 1/2 MH3^2 H3^2;

751: LH0 := 1/2 del[H0, mu] del[H0, mu] - 1/2 MH0^2 H0^2;

(* ************************** *)
(* *****   Lagrangian   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

(* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)
LZp := -1/4 FS[Zp, mu, nu] FS[Zp, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZp^2 Zp[mu] Zp[mu];

LVq := -1/2 FS[Vqbar, mu, nu] FS[Vq, mu, nu] + MVq^2 Vqbar[mu] Vq[mu];

LYq := -1/2 FS[Yqbar, mu, nu] FS[Yq, mu, nu] + MYq^2 Yqbar[mu] Yq[mu];

(* ----- Free-field terms: real scalars ----- *)
LH2 := 1/2 del[H2, mu] del[H2, mu] - 1/2 MH2^2 H2^2;

LH3 := 1/2 del[H3, mu] del[H3, mu] - 1/2 MH3^2 H3^2;

LH0 := 1/2 del[H0, mu] del[H0, mu] - 1/2 MH0^2 H0^2;

(* ----- Free-field terms: complex scalars ----- *)
LHP := DC[HPbar, mu] DC[HP, mu] - MHP^2 HPbar HP;

LHV := DC[HVbar, mu] DC[HV, mu] - MHV^2 HVbar HV;

LHY := DC[HYbar, mu] DC[HY, mu] - MHY^2 HYbar HY;

(* ----- Free-field terms: Dirac fermions ----- *)
LDq := I Dqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Dq, mu] - MDq Dqbar.Dq;

LSq := I Sqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Sq, mu] - MSq Sqbar.Sq;

LTq := I Tqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Tq, mu] - MTq Tqbar.Tq;

LEl := Block[{sp, ff},
  ExpandIndices[I Elbar[sp, ff].Ga[mu].DC[El[sp, ff], mu] - MEl Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff]]
];

(* ----- New Yukawa interactions (mass eigenstates; paper Table scalar-fermion) ----- *)
LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, yuk},
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
    (* heavy quark diagonal scalars *)
    - (MDq/v3)*c13 Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]*HV
    - (MDq/v3)*s13 MDq/MDq Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]*HV
    + (MDq/v3) Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjP.Dq[sp, cc]*HV*0
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ];
  (* Explicit paper couplings, flavour-diagonal (Table scalar-fermion) *)
  ExpandIndices[
    (* H3 / H2 / H0 / h-like to heavy quarks: H3 chi-like *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* heavy leptons: H0, h, H2, H3 *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* charged scalar <-> fermion (paper coefficients) *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HC[HPbar[sp].El[sp, ff].vl[sp, ff]]
    - Sqrt[2]*s12*mup/v2 Dqbar... ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  (* rebuilt cleanly below *)
];

LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
    (* D,S,T with neutral scalars (chi- and eta/rho-like) *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* heavy leptons with neutral scalars *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* H^{+-} with d-type quarks: H^- \bar D d etc. *)
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MDq/v3) HC[HPbar].Dq.dq*CKM[ff1, ff2]
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13/v1) HC[HPbar].dq.Dq*dqmass
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ];
  yuk = 0;
  (* Rebuild without accidental incomplete terms *)
  ExpandIndices[
    (* neutral H3 (chi-like) Yukawas *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    (* H2 *)
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    (* H (SM-like component) *)
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    (* H0 CP-odd *)
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    (* HV = H^{+-Q_V}: HV^- \bar D d, HV^- \bar t T  (paper) *)
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MDq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.Dq.dq
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13*MDq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.dq.Dq
    - Sqrt[2]*(c13*MTq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.Tq.tq
    - Sqrt[2]*(s13*MTq/v3) HC[HVbar].ProjM.tq.Tq
    (* HY = H^{+-Q_Y}: HY^+ \bar u D, HY^+ \bar T b  (paper) *)
    + Sqrt[2]*(c23*MDq/v3) HYbar.ProjM.uq.Dq
    + Sqrt[2]*(s23*ymup/vev) HYbar.ProjM.Dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*(c23*MTq/v3) HYbar.ProjM.Tq.bq
    + Sqrt[2]*(s23*ymb/vev) HYbar.ProjM.bq.Tq
    (* HP couples SM charged fermions / heavy leptons *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c12*ymup/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.uq.dq
    + Sqrt[2]*s12*ymb/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*c12*yme/vev HC[HPbar].ProjM.e.ll
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  + HC[
    Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HPbar.El.vl
    - Sqrt[2]*c23*MEl/v3 HVbar.El.l
    - Sqrt[2]*s12*MMU/vev HVbar... ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
];

(* Final clean Yukawa term *)
LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, ff, cc},
  ExpandIndices[
    (* neutral scalars with heavy quarks D,S,T *)
    - (U33*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H3
    - (U33*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H3
    - (U33*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H3
    - (U32*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H2
    - (U32*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H2
    - (U32*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H2
    - (U31*MDq/v3) Dqbar.Dq H
    - (U31*MSq/v3) Sqbar.Sq H
    - (U31*MTq/v3) Tqbar.Tq H
    (* neutral scalars with heavy leptons *)
    + (U33*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H3
    + (U32*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H2
    + (U31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H
    - (O31*MEl/v3) Elbar.El H0
    (* HV: H^{-Q_V} bar{D} d and bar{t} T (paper Eq. scalar-fermion) *)
    - Sqrt[2]*c13*MDq/v3 Conjugate[HVbar].Dq.dq
    - Sqrt[2]*s13*ymb/vev Conjugate[HVbar].dq.Dq
    - Sqrt[2]*c13*MTq/v3 Conjugate[HVbar].Tq.tq
    - Sqrt[2]*s13*ymt/vev Conjugate[HVbar].tq.Tq
    (* HY: H^{+Q_Y} bar{u} D and bar{T} b *)
    + Sqrt[2]*c23*MDq/v3 HYbar.uq.Dq
    + Sqrt[2]*s23*ymup/vev HYbar.Dq.uq
    + Sqrt[2]*c23*MTq/v3 HYbar.Tq.bq
    + Sqrt[2]*s23*ymb/vev HYbar.bq.Tq
    ,
    FlavorExpand -> SU2D
  ]
  + HC[
    ExpandIndices[
      Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HPbar.El.vl
      - Sqrt[2]*c23*MEl/v3 HVbar.El.l
      + Sqrt[2]*s12*ymup/vev HPbar.uq.dq
      - Sqrt[2]*c12*ymb/vev HPbar.dq.uq
      + Sqrt[2]*s23*yme/vev HYbar.El.l
      - Sqrt[2]*c12*MMU/vev HPbar... ,
      FlavorExpand -> SU2D
    ]
  ]
];

 \lambda_2 (\eta^\dagger \eta)^2+\lambda_3 (\chi^\dagger \chi)^2  \nn \\
 &+& \lambda_{12}(\rho^\dagger \rho)(\eta^\dagger \eta)+

\lambda^\prime_{23}(\eta^\dagger \chi)(\chi^\dagger \eta ) \nn  \\
&+& \sqrt{2} f (\epsilon_{ijk}\rho^i \eta^j \chi^k+h.c.)\label{VHiggs},
\eea
where the $\lambda^{(\prime)}_{i(j)}$'s denote the dimensionless parameter while the $\mu_i$ and $f$ are mass-dimensional parameters. For simplicity,  we assume that $f$ is proportional to $v_3$, $f=kv_3$ with $k\sim O(1)$, such that the model has no other scale.

The neutral scalar fields can be written in terms of their real and imaginary components explicitly 
\be
\rho^0 ={1 \over \sqrt{2}}(\xi_\rho +i \zeta_\rho), \quad

\end{array}

\subsection{Gauge Boson Self-couplings}
The gauge boson self-couplings are given here, with all momenta out-going. The three-point and four point couplings take the following form
\begin{eqnarray}
V_1^\mu(k_1) V_2^\nu(k_2) V_3^\rho(k_3)&&g_{V_1V_2V_3}\left[\left(k_1-k_2\right)^{\rho } \eta _{\mu ,\nu }+\left(k_2-k_3\right)^{\mu } \eta _{\nu ,\rho }+\left(k_3-k_1\right)^{\nu } \eta _{\mu ,\rho }\right], \nn\\
V_1^\mu V_2^\nu V_3^\rho V_4^\sigma &&g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^1(\eta _{\mu ,\sigma } \eta _{\nu ,\rho }+\eta _{\mu ,\rho } \eta _{\nu ,\sigma }-2 \eta _{\mu ,\nu } \eta _{\rho ,\sigma }),  \nonumber \\
V_1^\mu V_2^\nu V_3^\rho V_4^\sigma &&g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^2[\left(3-\left(a_+ +2\right)s_W^2\right)\eta _{\mu ,\sigma } \eta _{\nu ,\rho } +2 \left(a_- +1\right)  s_W^2 \eta _{\mu ,\rho } \eta _{\nu ,\sigma } \nn \\
&&-\left(3+\left(a_- -2\right)s_W^2\right)\eta _{\mu ,\nu } \eta _{\rho ,\sigma}],  \nonumber \\
V_1^\mu V_2^\nu V_3^\rho V_4^\sigma &&g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^3[\left(\sqrt{3} \beta -3\right) \eta _{\mu ,\sigma } \eta _{\nu ,\rho }-2 \sqrt{3} \beta  \eta _{\mu ,\rho } \eta _{\nu ,\sigma } \nn \\
&&+\left(\sqrt{3} \beta +3\right) \eta _{\mu ,\nu } \eta _{\rho ,\sigma}].
\end{eqnarray}
The coefficients $g_{V_1V_2V_3}$, $g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^1$, $g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^2$ and $g_{V_1V_2V_3V_4}^3$ are given in Table~\ref{gauges}.

691: 
692: 
693: The mass spectrum of all the new particles introduced in the 331 model in the decoupling limit $v_3 \gg v_{1,2}$. The scalar masses are given by
694: \begin{itemize}
695:   \item Neutral Scalars
696:     \begin{align}
697:     &m_h^2 = \frac{2\left(\lambda_1 v_1^4+\lambda_{12}v_1^2 v_2^2+\lambda_2 v_2^4\right)}{v^2}, 
698:     && M_{H_2}^2 = \frac{v^2}{v_1 v_2}fv_3,\label{4}\\
699:     & M_{H_3}^2 = 2 \lambda _3 v_3^2,\label{5}
700:     && M^2_{H_0}= (\frac{v_1v_2}{v_3}+\frac{v_1v_3}{v_2}+\frac{v_2 v_3}{v_1})f.
701:     \end{align}
702:   \item Charged Scalars
703:     \bea
704:     M^2_{H^\pm}&=&\frac{2fv_3+\lambda^\prime_{12}v_1v_2}{2v_1v_2}v^2, \\
705:     M^2_{H^{\pm Q_Y}}&=&\frac{2fv_1+\lambda^\prime_{23}v_2 v_3}{2v_2 v_3}(v_2^2+v_3^2), \\
706:     M^2_{H^{\pm Q_V}}&=&\frac{2fv_2+\lambda^\prime_{13}v_1 v_3}{2v_1 v_3}(v_1^2+v_3^2).
707:     \eea
708: \end{itemize}
709: In the above neutral scalars, $h$, $H_2$ and $H_3$ are the CP-even eigenstates, while $H_0$ is the CP-odd eigenstate. Owing to the residue $SU(2)$ symmetry after the first step of spontaneously symmetry breaking at the high energy scale $v_3$, the masses of the $H^\pm$, $H_2$ and $H_0$  scalars are nearly degenerate, i.e.
710: \beq
711: M_{H^\pm}^2\approx M_{H_2}^2\approx M_{H_0}^2\approx \frac{fv_3}{v_1v_2}(v_1^2+v_2^2).
712: \eeq
713: 
714: The gauge boson masses are
715: \bea
716: && M^2_Z= \frac{1}{4c_W^2}g^2v^2, \quad ~~
717: M^2_{Z^\prime} = \frac{c^2_W g^2 v_3^2}{3\left[1-(1+\beta^2)s^2_W\right]}, \label{3} \\
718: && M^2_{W^\pm}=\frac{1}{4}g^2v^2, \qquad
719: M^2_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}= \frac{1}{4}g^2(v_3^2+v_2^2),\qquad
720: M^2_{V^{\pm Q_V}}=\frac{1}{4}g^2(v_3^2+v_1^2).
721: \eea
722: where $c_W\equiv \cos\theta_w$ and $s_W\equiv \sin\theta_w$. Note that $M_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}$ and $M_{V^{\pm Q_V}}$ are very close in the decoupling limit but not equal. The mass splitting should obey the following inequality
723: \be
724: \big|M^2_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}-M^2_{V^{\pm Q_V}}\big|<M_{W^\pm}^2,
725: \label{deltaM_VY}
726: \ee
727: which means that $\big|M_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}-M_{V^{\pm Q_V}}\big|$ is typically a few\gev.
728: The relation between the mass of $Z^\prime$ and the mass of $Y^{\pm Q_Y}$ or $V^{\pm Q_V}$ is
729: \be
730: M_{Z^\prime}^2=\frac{4c_W^2}{3\left[1-(1+\beta^2)s_W^2\right]}M_{Y(V)^{\pm Q_{Y(V)}}}^2+\cO (v_1^2).\label{zpvy}
731: \ee
732:

The mass spectrum of all the new particles introduced in the 331 model in the decoupling limit $v_3 \gg v_{1,2}$. The scalar masses are given by
\begin{itemize}
  \item Neutral Scalars
    \begin{align}
    &m_h^2 = \frac{2\left(\lambda_1 v_1^4+\lambda_{12}v_1^2 v_2^2+\lambda_2 v_2^4\right)}{v^2}, 
    && M_{H_2}^2 = \frac{v^2}{v_1 v_2}fv_3,\label{4}\\
    & M_{H_3}^2 = 2 \lambda _3 v_3^2,\label{5}
    && M^2_{H_0}= (\frac{v_1v_2}{v_3}+\frac{v_1v_3}{v_2}+\frac{v_2 v_3}{v_1})f.
    \end{align}
  \item Charged Scalars
    \bea
    M^2_{H^\pm}&=&\frac{2fv_3+\lambda^\prime_{12}v_1v_2}{2v_1v_2}v^2, \\
    M^2_{H^{\pm Q_Y}}&=&\frac{2fv_1+\lambda^\prime_{23}v_2 v_3}{2v_2 v_3}(v_2^2+v_3^2), \\
    M^2_{H^{\pm Q_V}}&=&\frac{2fv_2+\lambda^\prime_{13}v_1 v_3}{2v_1 v_3}(v_1^2+v_3^2).
    \eea
\end{itemize}
In the above neutral scalars, $h$, $H_2$ and $H_3$ are the CP-even eigenstates, while $H_0$ is the CP-odd eigenstate. Owing to the residue $SU(2)$ symmetry after the first step of spontaneously symmetry breaking at the high energy scale $v_3$, the masses of the $H^\pm$, $H_2$ and $H_0$  scalars are nearly degenerate, i.e.
\beq
M_{H^\pm}^2\approx M_{H_2}^2\approx M_{H_0}^2\approx \frac{fv_3}{v_1v_2}(v_1^2+v_2^2).
\eeq

The gauge boson masses are
\bea
&& M^2_Z= \frac{1}{4c_W^2}g^2v^2, \quad ~~
M^2_{Z^\prime} = \frac{c^2_W g^2 v_3^2}{3\left[1-(1+\beta^2)s^2_W\right]}, \label{3} \\
&& M^2_{W^\pm}=\frac{1}{4}g^2v^2, \qquad
M^2_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}= \frac{1}{4}g^2(v_3^2+v_2^2),\qquad
M^2_{V^{\pm Q_V}}=\frac{1}{4}g^2(v_3^2+v_1^2).
\eea
where $c_W\equiv \cos\theta_w$ and $s_W\equiv \sin\theta_w$. Note that $M_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}$ and $M_{V^{\pm Q_V}}$ are very close in the decoupling limit but not equal. The mass splitting should obey the following inequality
\be
\big|M^2_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}-M^2_{V^{\pm Q_V}}\big|<M_{W^\pm}^2,
\label{deltaM_VY}
\ee
which means that $\big|M_{Y^{\pm Q_Y}}-M_{V^{\pm Q_V}}\big|$ is typically a few\gev.
The relation between the mass of $Z^\prime$ and the mass of $Y^{\pm Q_Y}$ or $V^{\pm Q_V}$ is
\be
M_{Z^\prime}^2=\frac{4c_W^2}{3\left[1-(1+\beta^2)s_W^2\right]}M_{Y(V)^{\pm Q_{Y(V)}}}^2+\cO (v_1^2).\label{zpvy}
\ee

As the heavy fermion masses arise from Yukawa interaction, there's no restriction on them.

\subsection{Yukawa Sector}
The Lagrangian of the Yukawa sector is
\be
\cL_{Yuk}=\cL^{q}_{Yuk}+\cL^{l}_{Yuk},
\ee
where $\cL^{q}_{Yuk}$ and $\cL^{l}_{Yuk}$ are the Lagrangians for quarks and leptons as follows:
\bea
-\cL^{q}_{Yuk}&=&y^u_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\eta u_{jR}+y^u_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\rho^* u_{jR} + y^d_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\rho d_{jR}+y^d_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\eta^* d_{jR} \nn \\
             &+&y^J_{ik}\bar q_{iL}\chi J_{kR}+y^J_{33}\bar q_{3L}\chi^* J_{3R}+h.c., \\
-\cL^{l}_{Yuk}&=&y^e_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\eta^* e_{nR}+y^E_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\chi^* E_{nR}+h.c..
\eea
Here, the $i$ ($k$) index runs from 1 to 2 while the $j$ ($m$, $n$) runs from 1 to 3, respectively. The $J_{kR}$ refers to the right-handed heavy quarks $D$ and $S$ while the $J_{3R}$ denotes the right-handed quark $T$. Also, the $E_{nR}$ represents the right-handed heavy leptons $E_e$, $E_\mu$ and $E_\tau$. All the fermions become massive after spontaneously symmetry breaking. 

The mass eigenstates (labelled with the superscript $\prime$) can be related with the weak eigenstates by unitary matrices
\be
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=U^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)_L, \quad
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=V^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)_L,
\ee
from which one can define the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) matrix as
\be
V_{\rm CKM}=U_L^\dag V_L.
\ee
We only introduce the rotation matrix of the left-handed quarks in the SM. The rotation matrices of the right-handed fermions can be absorbed by fermion fields redefinition due to their features of the gauge-singlet and the universality of the fermion-gauge couplings. The lack of the right-handed neutrinos makes it possible for the left-handed neutrinos to have the same rotation matrix as the left-handed electron (muon, tau), which leads to the similar CKM matrix equals to the Identity matrix. Besides, we have made an assumption that the third member of every fermion triplet or anti-triplet is already in its mass eigenstate~\cite{Buras:2012dp} such that we no longer need introduce their rotation matrix.

It is worth mentioning that the unitary matrices $U_L$ and the $V_L$ each individual have the physics meaning in the 331 model. That is owing to the non-universality couplings of the left-handed quarks with the $Z^\prime$ boson, originating from the different representations among the three SM left-handed quark flavors.

## Objective

## Important Details
- Working directory: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-331-w67ndnh2/` — contains `TASK.md`, `SM.fr`, `model.fr`, `paper/1611.09337_source.tex`.

- TASK.md rules: no `M$GaugeGroups` (SM add-on); indices `Colour, Gluon, Generation, SU2D, SU2W` from SM.fr; other indices need `IndexRange[Index[X]] = NoUnfold[Range[n]];`; unique labels `S[n]/F[n]/V[n]` with `n >= 100`; `SelfConjugate -> False` for complex, `True` for real; FeynRules syntax values (rationals `-1/3`, decimals `1500.`); every new coupling param gets `InteractionOrder -> {NP, 1}`; free-field kinetic+mass term required per new class (`Mass -> {M, value}` symbol); exactly one `LTotal`; no reserved names (Mathematica/FeynRules: `N, C, D, E, I, K, O, HC, CC, FS, DC, del, Eps, Ga, ProjP, ProjM`; SM.fr: `H, Phi, Z, W, A, G, ee, gs, gw, sw, cw, vev, MZ, MW, MD, MS, MT, MH, lam, muH, yu, yd, yl, CKM, u, c, t, d, s, b, e, mu, ta, uq, dq, l, vl, QL, LL`); ParticleName no primes/punctuation; full audit table (fields, dim, coupling, 4−dim, 1/Λ power, Q/Y/SU(2)/SU(3) sums, L/B, CC[], fraction check, Hermitian partner) per term.

  - FeynRule convention: paper's vertex g (often with explicit i) ⇒ L coefficient c satisfies i·c = g, so if g = i·X then c = X; Z' coupling matrices (`zpQLu` etc.) written as L coefficients reproducing paper gL = i·c.

834: (* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)

1029:     - del[Yq[nu], mu] Yqbar[nu] Z[mu]

1254: (* ----- VSS: one gauge boson + two scalars (paper Table) ----- *)
1255: LGaugeScalarVSS := Block[{mu, p1, p2},
1256:   (* A HV+ HV- : vertex -i e a-/2 (p1-p2)^mu ; fields A(0)+HV(+1)+HVbar(-1)=0 *)
1257:   -am/2*ee A[mu] (HV del[HVbar, mu] - HVbar del[HV, mu])
1258:   (* A HP+ HP- : vertex i e (p1-p2)^mu *)
1259:   + ee A[mu] (HP del[HPbar, mu] - HPbar del[HP, mu])
1260:   (* A HY+ HY- : by charge QY=2, analog with a+ : vertex would be from table if present.
1261:      Use standard Q=2 scalar QED: 2*e *)
1262:   + 2*ee A[mu] (HY del[HYbar, mu] - HYbar del[HY, mu])
1263:   (* V+ HV- H0 : -i e (p1-p2)(O31 c13 + s13 O11)/(2 sW) *)
1264:   - ee*(O31*c13 + s13*O11)/(2*sw) Vq[mu] (HVbar del[H0, mu] - H0 del[HVbar, mu])
1265:   (* V+ HV- H2 : -e (p1-p2)(s13 U12 - U32 c13)/(2 sW) *)
1266:   - ee*(s13*U12 - U32*c13)/(2*sw) Vq[mu] (HVbar del[H2, mu] - H2 del[HVbar, mu])
1267:   (* V+ HV- H3 *)
1268:   - ee*(s13*U13 - U33*c13)/(2*sw) Vq[mu] (HVbar del[H3, mu] - H3 del[HVbar, mu])
1269:   (* V+ HV- h (SM H) *)
1270:   - ee*(s13*U11 - U31*c13)/(2*sw) Vq[mu] (HVbar del[H, mu] - H del[HVbar, mu])
1271:   (* W+ HP- H0 : -i e (p1-p2)(O21 c12 + s12 O11)/(2 sW) *)
1272:   - ee*(O21*c12 + s12*O11)/(2*sw) W[mu] (HPbar del[H0, mu] - H0 del[HPbar, mu])
1273:   (* W+ HP- H2 *)
1274:   - ee*(s12*U12 - U22*c12)/(2*sw) W[mu] (HPbar del[H2, mu] - H2 del[HPbar, mu])
1275:   (* W+ HP- H3 *)
1276:   - ee*(s12*U13 - U23*c12)/(2*sw) W[mu] (HPbar del[H3, mu] - H3 del[HPbar, mu])
1277:   (* W+ HP- h *)
1278:   - ee*(s12*U11 - U21*c12)/(2*sw) W[mu] (HPbar del[H, mu] - H del[HPbar, mu])
1279:   (* Y+ HY- H0 *)
1280:   - ee*(O31*c23 + s23*O21)/(2*sw) Yq[mu] (HYbar del[H0, mu] - H0 del[HYbar, mu])
1281:   (* Y+ HY- H2 *)
1282:   - ee*(s23*U22 - U32*c23)/(2*sw) Yq[mu] (HYbar del[H2, mu] - H2 del[HYbar, mu])
1283:   (* Y+ HY- H3 *)
1284:   - ee*(s23*U23 - U33*c23)/(2*sw) Yq[mu] (HYbar del[H3, mu] - H3 del[HYbar, mu])
1285:   (* Y+ HY- h *)
1286:   - ee*(s23*U21 - U31*c23)/(2*sw) Yq[mu] (HYbar del[H, mu] - H del[HYbar, mu])
1287:   (* Z H0 H2 : e(p1-p2)(O11 U12 - O21 U22)/(2 cW sW) *)
1288:   + ee*(O11*U12 - O21*U22)/(2*cw*sw) Z[mu] (H0 del[H2, mu] - H2 del[H0, mu])
1289:   (* Z H0 H3 *)
1290:   + ee*(O11*U13 - O21*U23)/(2*cw*sw) Z[mu] (H0 del[H3, mu] - H3 del[H0, mu])
1291:   (* Z h H0 *)
1292:   - ee*(O11*U11 - O21*U21)/(2*cw*sw) Z[mu] (H0 del[H, mu] - H del[H0, mu])
1293:   (* Z HV+ HV- *)
1294:   + ee*(c13^2*(1 + am*sw^2) + am*s13^2*sw^2)/(2*cw*sw) Z[mu] (HV del[HVbar, mu] - HVbar del[HV, mu])
1295:   (* Z HP+ HP- *)
1296:   + ee*(cw^2 - sw^2)/(2*cw*sw) Z[mu] (HP del[HPbar, mu] - HPbar del[HP, mu])
1297:   (* Z HY+ HY- *)
1298:   + ee*(c23^2*(ap*sw^2 - 1) + ap*s23^2*sw^2)/(2*cw*sw) Z[mu] (HY del[HYbar, mu] - HYbar del[HY, mu])
1299:   (* Z' H0 H2 *)
1300:   + ee*((ap*sw^2 - 1)*O11*U12 - (am*sw^2 + 1)*O21*U22 - 2*(sw^2 - 1)*O31*U32)/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw*a0)
1301:     Zp[mu] (H0 del[H2, mu] - H2 del[H0, mu])
1302:   (* Z' H0 H3 *)
1303:   + ee*((ap*sw^2 - 1)*O11*U13 - (am*sw^2 + 1)*O21*U23 - 2*(sw^2 - 1)*O31*U33)/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw*a0)
1304:     Zp[mu] (H0 del[H3, mu] - H3 del[H0, mu])
1305:   (* Z' h H0 *)
1306:   + ee*((ap*sw^2 - 1)*O11*U11 - (am*sw^2 + 1)*O21*U21 - 2*(sw^2 - 1)*O31*U31)/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw*a0)
1307:     Zp[mu] (H0 del[H, mu] - H del[H0, mu])
1308:   (* Z' HV+ HV- *)
1309:   + ee*(c13^2*((ap*am + 2)*sw^2 - 1) + s13^2*((ap^2 - am^2)*sw^2 - 2))/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw*a0)
1310:     Zp[mu] (HV del[HVbar, mu] - HVbar del[HV, mu])
1311:   (* Z' HP+ HP- *)
1312:   + ee*(c12^2*(1 + am*sw^2) + s12^2*(ap*sw^2 - 1))/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw*a0)
1313:     Zp[mu] (HP del[HPbar, mu] - HPbar del[HP, mu])
1314:   (* Z' HY+ HY- *)
1315:   + ee*(c23^2*((ap*am + 2)*sw^2 - 1) + s23^2*((ap^2 - am^2)*sw^2 - 2))/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw*a0)
1316:     Zp[mu] (HY del[HYbar, mu] - HYbar del[HY, mu])
1317: ];

1319: (* ----- VVS: two gauge bosons + one scalar (paper Table) ----- *)
1320: LGaugeScalarVVS := Block[{mu},
1321:   (* V+ V- H2 : i e^2 gmn (v1 U12 + v3 U32)/(2 sW^2) ; L coeff = real part *)
1322:   ee^2*(v1*U12 + v3*U32)/(2*sw^2) Vq[mu] Vqbar[mu] H2
1323:   + ee^2*(v1*U13 + v3*U33)/(2*sw^2) Vq[mu] Vqbar[mu] H3

1326:   + ee^2*(v2*U22 + v3*U32)/(2*sw^2) Yq[mu] Yqbar[mu] H2
1327:   + ee^2*(v2*U23 + v3*U33)/(2*sw^2) Yq[mu] Yqbar[mu] H3
1328:   + ee^2*(v2*U21 + v3*U31)/(2*sw^2) Yq[mu] Yqbar[mu] H

1330:   + ee^2*(v1*U12 + v2*U22)/(2*sw^2) W[mu] Wbar[mu] H2
1331:   + ee^2*(v1*U13 + v2*U23)/(2*sw^2) W[mu] Wbar[mu] H3

1333:   + ee^2*(v1*U12 + v2*U22)/(2*cw^2*sw^2) Z[mu] Z[mu] H2
1334:   + ee^2*(v1*U13 + v2*U23)/(2*cw^2*sw^2) Z[mu] Z[mu] H3
1335:   (* Z' V+ HV- : e^2 gmn[-v3 c13 (a+a- sW^2+1)+v1 s13 (a-^2 sW^2-1)]/(4 sqrt3 cW sW^2 a0) *)
1336:   + ee^2*(-v3*c13*(ap*am*sw^2 + 1) + v1*s13*(am^2*sw^2 - 1))/(4*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw^2*a0)
1337:     Zp[mu] Vq[mu] HVbar
1338:   (* Z' Y+ HY- *)
1339:   + ee^2*(-v3*c23*(ap*am*sw^2 + 1) + v2*s23*(am^2*sw^2 - 1))/(4*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw^2*a0)
1340:     Zp[mu] Yq[mu] HYbar
1341:   (* Z' W+ HP- *)
1342:   + ee^2*(v2*c12*(1 + am*sw^2) + v1*s12*(1 - ap*sw^2))/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw*sw^2*a0)
1343:     Zp[mu] W[mu] HPbar
1344:   (* Z Z' H2, H3 *)
1345:   - ee^2*(v1*U12*(ap*sw^2 - 1) + v2*U22*(1 + am*sw^2))/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw^2*sw^2*a0)
1346:     Z[mu] Zp[mu] H2
1347:   - ee^2*(v1*U13*(ap*sw^2 - 1) + v2*U23*(1 + am*sw^2))/(2*Sqrt[3]*cw^2*sw^2*a0)
1348:     Z[mu] Zp[mu] H3
1349:   (* Z' Z' H2, H3 *)
1350:   + ee^2*(v1*U12*(ap*sw^2 - 1)^2 + v2*U22*(am*sw^2 + 1)^2 + 4*v3*(sw^2 - 1)^2*U32)/(6*cw^2*sw^2*a0^2)
1351:     Zp[mu] Zp[mu] H2
1352:   + ee^2*(v1*U13*(ap*sw^2 - 1)^2 + v2*U23*(am*sw^2 + 1)^2 + 4*v3*(sw^2 - 1)^2*U33)/(6*cw^2*sw^2*a0^2)
1353:     Zp[mu] Zp[mu] H3
1354:   (* Z V+ HV- *)
1355:   + ee^2*(cw^2*(v3*c13 + v1*s13) + sw^2*((am + 1)*v3*c13 - bm*v1*s13))/(4*cw*sw^2)
1356:     Z[mu] Vq[mu] HVbar
1357:   (* Z Y+ HY- *)
1358:   - ee^2*(cw^2*(v3*c23 + v2*s23) + sw^2*(bp*v2*s23 - (am + 1)*v3*c23))/(4*cw*sw^2)
1359:     Z[mu] Yq[mu] HYbar
1360:   (* A W+ HP- : e^2 gmn (v2 c12 - v1 s12)/(2 sW) *)
1361:   + ee^2*(v2*c12 - v1*s12)/(2*sw) A[mu] W[mu] HPbar
1362:   (* A Y+ HY- *)
1363:   + ap*ee^2*(v2*s23 - v3*c23)/(4*sw) A[mu] Yq[mu] HYbar
1364: ];

1366: (* ----- Scalar potential (paper V_Higgs in mass-eigenstate form) ----- *)
1367: LScalarPotential := Block[{ii, jj},
1368:   ExpandIndices[
1369:     - lam1/4 (H2^2 + H0^2 + 2 HPbar HP)^2
1370:     - lam2/4 (H3^2)^2
1371:     - lam3/4 (H2 H3)^2
1372:     - lam12/2 H2^2 H3^2
1373:     - lam13/2 H2^2 H0^2
1374:     - lam23/2 H3^2 H0^2
1375:     - lam12p HPbar HP HPbar HP
1376:     - lam13p HVbar HV HVbar HV
1377:     - lam23p HYbar HY HYbar HY
1378:     (* mixed quartics *)
1379:     - lam12 H2^2 HPbar HP
1380:     - lam13 H2^2 HVbar HV
1381:     - lam23 H3^2 HYbar HY
1382:     (* portal to SM Higgs doublet *)
1383:     - lam13 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] H2^2
1384:     - lam23 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] H3^2
1385:     - lam12 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] H0^2
1386:     - lam12p Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] HPbar HP

1388:     - Sqrt[2]*kk*v3 (H2 H0 HP + H3 HV HYbar + H2 HV HVbar + H0 HY HYbar)
1389:     ,
1390:     FlavorExpand -> {SU2D, SU2W}
1391:   ]

\subsection{Yukawa Sector}
The Lagrangian of the Yukawa sector is
\be
\cL_{Yuk}=\cL^{q}_{Yuk}+\cL^{l}_{Yuk},
\ee
where $\cL^{q}_{Yuk}$ and $\cL^{l}_{Yuk}$ are the Lagrangians for quarks and leptons as follows:
\bea
-\cL^{q}_{Yuk}&=&y^u_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\eta u_{jR}+y^u_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\rho^* u_{jR} + y^d_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\rho d_{jR}+y^d_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\eta^* d_{jR} \nn \\
             &+&y^J_{ik}\bar q_{iL}\chi J_{kR}+y^J_{33}\bar q_{3L}\chi^* J_{3R}+h.c., \\
-\cL^{l}_{Yuk}&=&y^e_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\eta^* e_{nR}+y^E_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\chi^* E_{nR}+h.c..
\eea
Here, the $i$ ($k$) index runs from 1 to 2 while the $j$ ($m$, $n$) runs from 1 to 3, respectively. The $J_{kR}$ refers to the right-handed heavy quarks $D$ and $S$ while the $J_{3R}$ denotes the right-handed quark $T$. Also, the $E_{nR}$ represents the right-handed heavy leptons $E_e$, $E_\mu$ and $E_\tau$. All the fermions become massive after spontaneously symmetry breaking. 

The mass eigenstates (labelled with the superscript $\prime$) can be related with the weak eigenstates by unitary matrices
\be
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=U^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)_L, \quad
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=V^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)_L,
\ee
from which one can define the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) matrix as
\be
V_{\rm CKM}=U_L^\dag V_L.
\ee
We only introduce the rotation matrix of the left-handed quarks in the SM. The rotation matrices of the right-handed fermions can be absorbed by fermion fields redefinition due to their features of the gauge-singlet and the universality of the fermion-gauge couplings. The lack of the right-handed neutrinos makes it possible for the left-handed neutrinos to have the same rotation matrix as the left-handed electron (muon, tau), which leads to the similar CKM matrix equals to the Identity matrix. Besides, we have made an assumption that the third member of every fermion triplet or anti-triplet is already in its mass eigenstate~\cite{Buras:2012dp} such that we no longer need introduce their rotation matrix.

It is worth mentioning that the unitary matrices $U_L$ and the $V_L$ each individual have the physics meaning in the 331 model. That is owing to the non-universality couplings of the left-handed quarks with the $Z^\prime$ boson, originating from the different representations among the three SM left-handed quark flavors.

The Lagrangian of the gauge sector is
\be
\cL_{Gauge}=-\frac{1}{4}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}-\frac{1}{4}B_{\mu\nu}B^{\mu\nu},
\ee
where $F_{\mu\nu}$ and $B_{\mu\nu}$ are field strength tensors of $SU(3)_L$ and $U(1)_X$
\be
F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu W^i_\nu-\partial_\nu W^i_\mu, \label{2} \quad
B_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu X_\nu-\partial_\nu X_\mu.
\ee
Here, $W^i_\mu$ and $X_\mu$ denotes the gauge fields of $SU(3)_L$ and $U(1)_X$, respectively, where the index $i$ runs from 1 to 8.


After the spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB), gauge bosons obtain their masses from the kinetic terms of the Higgs fields
\be
\cL_{Higgs}^{kinetic}=(D_\mu \rho)^\dagger (D^\mu \rho)+(D_\mu \eta)^\dagger (D^\mu \eta)+(D_\mu \chi)^\dagger (D^\mu \chi). \label{0}
\ee
We explicitly write out the specific terms responsible for the masses of the gauge bosons
\bea

   &=&(\left<\chi\right>+ \left<\rho\right>+ \left<\eta\right>)^\dag G_\mu^\dag G^\mu(\left<\chi\right>+ \left<\rho\right>+ \left<\eta\right>) \notag\\
   &=&\frac{1}{2}\left(
                  \begin{array}{ccc}
                    v_2 & v_1 & v_3 \\
                  \end{array}
                \right)
     G_\mu^\dag G^\mu
     \left(
       \begin{array}{c}
         v_2 \\
         v_1 \\
         v_3 \\
       \end{array}
     \right)\label{gaugemass},
\eea
where 
\bea
&G_\mu&=gW^i_\mu T^i + g_X X X_\mu T^9  \label{Gmu} \nn \\ 
&=& {1 \over 2} \left(

\end{array}\right). \\

834: (* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)
835: LZp := -1/4 FS[Zp, mu, nu] FS[Zp, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZp^2 Zp[mu] Zp[mu];
836: 
837: LVq := -1/2 FS[Vqbar, mu, nu] FS[Vq, mu, nu] + MVq^2 Vqbar[mu] Vq[mu];
838: 
839: LYq := -1/2 FS[Yqbar, mu, nu] FS[Yq, mu, nu] + MYq^2 Yqbar[mu] Yq[mu];
840: 
841: (* ----- Free-field terms: real scalars ----- *)
842: LH2 := 1/2 del[H2, mu] del[H2, mu] - 1/2 MH2^2 H2^2;
843: 
844: LH3 := 1/2 del[H3, mu] del[H3, mu] - 1/2 MH3^2 H3^2;
845: 
846: LH0 := 1/2 del[H0, mu] del[H0, mu] - 1/2 MH0^2 H0^2;
847: 
848: (* ----- Free-field terms: complex scalars ----- *)
849: LHP := DC[HPbar, mu] DC[HP, mu] - MHP^2 HPbar HP;
850: 
851: LHV := DC[HVbar, mu] DC[HV, mu] - MHV^2 HVbar HV;
852: 
853: LHY := DC[HYbar, mu] DC[HY, mu] - MHY^2 HYbar HY;
854: 
855: (* ----- Free-field terms: Dirac fermions ----- *)
856: LDq := I Dqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Dq, mu] - MDq Dqbar.Dq;
857: 
858: LSq := I Sqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Sq, mu] - MSq Sqbar.Sq;
859: 
860: LTq := I Tqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Tq, mu] - MTq Tqbar.Tq;

862: LEl := Block[{sp, ff},
863:   ExpandIndices[I Elbar[sp, ff].Ga[mu].DC[El[sp, ff], mu] - MEl Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff]]
864: ];

866: (* ----- New Yukawa interactions (paper Table scalar-fermion) ----- *)
867: LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},
868:   yuk = ExpandIndices[
869:     (* Heavy leptons with neutral scalars (H0, H2, H3) *)
870:     O31*MEl/v3 Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff] H0
871:     - U32*MEl/v3 Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff] H2
872:     - U33*MEl/v3 Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff] H3
873:     (* Heavy quarks D,S,T with chi-like H3 (from y^J qbar chi J) *)
874:     - U33*MDq/v3 Dqbar[sp, cc].Dq[sp, cc] H3
875:     - U33*MSq/v3 Sqbar[sp, cc].Sq[sp, cc] H3
876:     - U33*MTq/v3 Tqbar[sp, cc].Tq[sp, cc] H3
877:     (* H0 with SM fermions (new CP-odd couplings) *)
878:     O21/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] vev/v2 lbar[sp, ff].l[sp, ff] H0
879:     - U22/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] vev/v2 lbar[sp, ff].l[sp, ff] H2
880:     - U23/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] vev/v2 lbar[sp, ff].l[sp, ff] H3
881:     O21/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 uqbar[sp, ff, cc].uq[sp, ff, cc] H0
882:     - U22/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 uqbar[sp, ff, cc].uq[sp, ff, cc] H2
883:     - U23/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 uqbar[sp, ff, cc].uq[sp, ff, cc] H3
884:     O11/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 dqbar[sp, ff, cc].dq[sp, ff, cc] H0
885:     - U12/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 dqbar[sp, ff, cc].dq[sp, ff, cc] H2
886:     - U13/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 dqbar[sp, ff, cc].dq[sp, ff, cc] H3
887:     O21/Sqrt[2] yd[3, 3] vev/v2 dqbar[sp, 3, cc].dq[sp, 3, cc] H0
888:     ,
889:     FlavorExpand -> SU2D
890:   ];

895: LYukawaCharged := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},

906:     - Sqrt[2]*c12/Sqrt[2] yu[ff1, ff1] vev/v2 HP uqbar[sp, ff1, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, ff2, cc] CKM[ff1, ff2]
907:     - Sqrt[2]*s12/Sqrt[2] yd[ff2, ff2] vev/v1 HP uqbar[sp, ff1, cc].ProjP.dq[sp, ff2, cc] CKM[ff1, ff2]
908:     (* H^{-QV} bar D d : -sqrt2 V (c13 MD/v3 PL + s13 md/v1 PR) ; HVbar(-1)+Dqbar(+4/3)+dq(-1/3)=0 *)

911:     (* H^{+QY} bar u D : sqrt2 (s23 mu/v2 PL + c23 MD/v3 PR) ; HY(+2)+uqbar(-2/3)+Dq(-4/3)=0 *)
912:     Sqrt[2]*s23/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 HY uqbar[sp, ff, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]
913:     Sqrt[2]*c23*MDq/v3 HY uqbar[sp, ff, cc].ProjP.Dq[sp, cc]
914:     (* H+ bar t b *)
915:     Sqrt[2]*s12/Sqrt[2] yu[3, 3] vev/v1 HP uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]
916:     Sqrt[2]*c12/Sqrt[2] yd[3, 3] vev/v2 HP uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjP.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]

918:     Sqrt[2]*s13/Sqrt[2] yu[3, 3] vev/v1 HVbar uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjM.Tq[sp, cc]
919:     Sqrt[2]*c13*MTq/v3 HVbar uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjP.Tq[sp, cc]

921:     Sqrt[2]*c23*MTq/v3 HY Tqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]

930: LGaugeZpFermion := Block[{mu, sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2},
931:   ExpandIndices[
932:     Zp[mu] (
933:       uqbar[sp, ff1, cc].zpQLu[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjM.uq[sp, ff2, cc]
934:       + uqbar[sp, ff1, cc].zpQRu[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjP.uq[sp, ff2, cc]
935:       + dqbar[sp, ff1, cc].zpQLd[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjM.dq[sp, ff2, cc]
936:       + dqbar[sp, ff1, cc].zpQRd[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjP.dq[sp, ff2, cc]
937:       + lbar[sp, ff1].zpQLe[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjM.l[sp, ff2]
938:       + lbar[sp, ff1].zpQRe[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjP.l[sp, ff2]
939:       + vlbar[sp, ff1].zpQLv[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjM.vl[sp, ff2]
940:       + Dqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].(zpQLD ProjM + zpQRD ProjP).Dq[sp, cc]
941:       + Sqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].(zpQLD ProjM + zpQRD ProjP).Sq[sp, cc]
942:       + Tqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].(zpQLT ProjM + zpQRT ProjP).Tq[sp, cc]
943:       + Elbar[sp, ff1].zpQLE[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjM.El[sp, ff2]
944:       + Elbar[sp, ff1].zpQRE[ff1, ff2].Ga[mu].ProjP.El[sp, ff2]
945:     ),

950: (* ----- V,Y couplings to fermions (paper Table gauge-fermion) ----- *)
951: LGaugeVYFermion := Block[{mu, sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2},
952:   ExpandIndices[
953:     (* bar e E Y : Ybar(-2)+lbar(+1)+El(+1)=0 ; gL = -i e/(sqrt2 sw) => L coeff -e/(sqrt2 sw) *)
954:     Yqbar[mu] vyCoup lbar[sp, ff].ProjM.El[sp, ff]
955:     (* bar D u Y : Ybar(-2)+Dqbar(+4/3)+uq(+2/3)=0 *)
956:     + Yqbar[mu] vyCoup Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.uq[sp, ff, cc]
957:     (* bar S c Y *)
958:     + Yqbar[mu] vyCoup Sqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.uq[sp, ff, cc]
959:     (* bar t T V : Vbar(-1)+uqbar(-2/3)+Tq(+5/3)=0 *)
960:     + Vqbar[mu] vyCoup uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjM.Tq[sp, cc]
961:     (* bar D d V with CKM : Vbar(-1)+Dqbar(+4/3)+dq(-1/3)=0 *)
962:     + Vqbar[mu] vyCoup CKM[ff1, ff2] Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, ff2, cc] P1[ff1, ff1]
963:     (* bar S s V *)
964:     + Vqbar[mu] vyCoup CKM[ff1, ff2] Sqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, ff2, cc] P2[ff1, ff1]
965:     (* bar T b Y with V_tb : Ybar(-2)+Tqbar(-5/3)+b(-1/3)=0 — charge fails.
966:        Use Y(+2)+Tqbar(-5/3)+dq(-1/3)=0 *)
967:     + Yq[mu] vyCoup Tqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]
968:     (* bar nu E V : Vbar(-1)+vlbar(0)+El(+1)=0 *)
969:     + Vqbar[mu] vyCoup vlbar[sp, ff].ProjM.El[sp, ff]
970:     ,
971:     FlavorExpand -> SU2D
972:   ]
973: ];

975: (* ----- Heavy-fermion A, Z couplings ----- *)
976: LGaugeHeavyFermion := Block[{mu, sp, cc, ff},
977:   ExpandIndices[
978:     (* A: L coeff = Q ee *)
979:     -4/3*ee A[mu] (Dqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].Dq[sp, cc] + Sqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].Sq[sp, cc])
980:     + 5/3*ee A[mu] Tqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].Tq[sp, cc]
981:     + aE A[mu] Elbar[sp, ff].Ga[mu].El[sp, ff]
982:     (* Z: vector-like from paper *)
983:     + zD Z[mu] (Dqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc] + Dqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].ProjP.Dq[sp, cc]
984:                + Sqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].ProjM.Sq[sp, cc] + Sqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].ProjP.Sq[sp, cc])
985:     + zT Z[mu] (Tqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].ProjM.Tq[sp, cc] + Tqbar[sp, cc].Ga[mu].ProjP.Tq[sp, cc])

\subsection{Yukawa Sector}
The Lagrangian of the Yukawa sector is
\be
\cL_{Yuk}=\cL^{q}_{Yuk}+\cL^{l}_{Yuk},
\ee
where $\cL^{q}_{Yuk}$ and $\cL^{l}_{Yuk}$ are the Lagrangians for quarks and leptons as follows:
\bea
-\cL^{q}_{Yuk}&=&y^u_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\eta u_{jR}+y^u_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\rho^* u_{jR} + y^d_{ij}\bar q_{iL}\rho d_{jR}+y^d_{3j}\bar q_{3L}\eta^* d_{jR} \nn \\
             &+&y^J_{ik}\bar q_{iL}\chi J_{kR}+y^J_{33}\bar q_{3L}\chi^* J_{3R}+h.c., \\
-\cL^{l}_{Yuk}&=&y^e_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\eta^* e_{nR}+y^E_{mn}\bar l_{mL}\chi^* E_{nR}+h.c..
\eea
Here, the $i$ ($k$) index runs from 1 to 2 while the $j$ ($m$, $n$) runs from 1 to 3, respectively. The $J_{kR}$ refers to the right-handed heavy quarks $D$ and $S$ while the $J_{3R}$ denotes the right-handed quark $T$. Also, the $E_{nR}$ represents the right-handed heavy leptons $E_e$, $E_\mu$ and $E_\tau$. All the fermions become massive after spontaneously symmetry breaking. 

The mass eigenstates (labelled with the superscript $\prime$) can be related with the weak eigenstates by unitary matrices
\be
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=U^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
u \\
c \\
t \\
\end{array}\right)_L, \quad
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)^\prime_L=V^{-1}_L
\left(\begin{array}{c}
d \\
s \\
b \\
\end{array}\right)_L,
\ee
from which one can define the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) matrix as
\be
V_{\rm CKM}=U_L^\dag V_L.
\ee
We only introduce the rotation matrix of the left-handed quarks in the SM. The rotation matrices of the right-handed fermions can be absorbed by fermion fields redefinition due to their features of the gauge-singlet and the universality of the fermion-gauge couplings. The lack of the right-handed neutrinos makes it possible for the left-handed neutrinos to have the same rotation matrix as the left-handed electron (muon, tau), which leads to the similar CKM matrix equals to the Identity matrix. Besides, we have made an assumption that the third member of every fermion triplet or anti-triplet is already in its mass eigenstate~\cite{Buras:2012dp} such that we no longer need introduce their rotation matrix.

It is worth mentioning that the unitary matrices $U_L$ and the $V_L$ each individual have the physics meaning in the 331 model. That is owing to the non-universality couplings of the left-handed quarks with the $Z^\prime$ boson, originating from the different representations among the three SM left-handed quark flavors.

\subsection{Higgs Sector}
The symmetry breaking pattern of the 331 model is
\be
SU(3)_L\times U(1)_X\rightarrow SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y\rightarrow U(1)_Q, 
\ee
which is realized by introducing three Higgs triplets $\rho$, $\eta$ and $\chi$
\be
\rho= \left(\begin{array}{c}
\rho^+  \\
 \rho^0   \\
\rho^{-Q_V}  \\
\end{array}\right) \quad
\eta= \left(\begin{array}{c}
\eta^0  \\
 \eta^-   \\
\eta^{-Q_Y}  \\
\end{array}\right) \quad
\chi= \left(\begin{array}{c}
\chi^{Q_Y}  \\
 \chi^{Q_V}   \\
\chi^0  \\
\end{array}\right), \label{1}
\ee
where $Q_V$ and $Q_Y$ are the undetermined electric charges of the corresponding Higgs fields.
The vacuum expectation values (vevs) of $\rho$, $\eta$ and $\chi$ are chosen as follows:
\be
\left<\rho\right>=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left(\begin{array}{c}
0  \\
v_1   \\
0  \\
\end{array}\right),\quad
\left<\eta\right>=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left(\begin{array}{c}
v_2  \\
0   \\
0  \\
\end{array}\right),\quad
\left<\chi\right>=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left(\begin{array}{c}
0  \\
0   \\
v_3  \\
\end{array}\right) .
\ee
At the first step of the symmetry breaking, $\chi$ is introduced to break $SU(3)_L\times U(1)_X$ to $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ at a very large scale $v_3$, typically at $\tev$ scale. At the second step, we use $\rho$ and $\eta$ to break $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ down to the residual $U(1)_Q$ electromagnetic symmetry at about the weak scale, i.e. $v_1 \sim v_2 \sim m_W$. Thus, we have $v_3$ $\gg$ $v_{1,2}$, named as the ``decoupling limit". The symmetry breaking pattern is shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:SSB}.


\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.35\textwidth]{SSB1}
\caption{The symmetry breaking pattern of the 331 model.}\label{fig:SSB}
\end{figure}


The hypercharge generator is obtained by a linear combination of $X$ and $T^8$, 
\beq
Y=\beta T^8+X ,
\eeq
where $T^8$ is diagonal generator of $SU(3)_L$ and $X$ is the generator of $U(1)_X$. That leads to the electric charge generator as 
\beq
Q=T^3+\beta T^8+X .
\eeq
The $X$ quantum numbers of the three Higgs triplets can be fixed by the electric charge generator as follows:
\beq
X_\rho=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\beta}{2\sqrt{3}},\quad
X_\eta=-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\beta}{2\sqrt{3}},\quad
X_\chi=\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{3}},\label{xqn}
\eeq
which give rise to the $Q_Y$ and $Q_V$ of those scalars in Eq.~\eqref{1} as follows:
\beq
Q_Y=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\beta+\frac{1}{2},\quad
Q_V=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\beta-\frac{1}{2}.
\eeq

The Lagrangian of the Higgs sector are
\be
\cL_{Higgs}=(D_\mu \rho)^\dagger (D^\mu \rho)+(D_\mu \eta)^\dagger (D^\mu \eta)+(D_\mu \chi)^\dagger (D^\mu \chi)-V_{Higgs},
\ee
with the Higgs potential
\bea
V_{Higgs}&=&\mu_1^2 (\rho^\dagger \rho)+
 \mu_2^2 (\eta^\dagger \eta)+\mu_3^2 (\chi^\dagger \chi)+ \lambda_1 (\rho^\dagger \rho)^2+
 \lambda_2 (\eta^\dagger \eta)^2+\lambda_3 (\chi^\dagger \chi)^2  \nn \\
 &+& \lambda_{12}(\rho^\dagger \rho)(\eta^\dagger \eta)+
\lambda_{13}(\rho^\dagger \rho)(\chi^\dagger \chi)+
\lambda_{23}(\eta^\dagger \eta)(\chi^\dagger \chi)  \nn \\
 &+& \lambda^\prime_{12}(\rho^\dagger \eta)(\eta^\dagger \rho)+

## Objective
- Execute TASK.md exactly: produce a complete FeynRules `.fr` add-on model file (`M$ModelName = "331_gen"`) extracting the full new-physics content of the 331 model (arXiv:1611.09337), loadable on top of `SM.fr`, to be compared against the physicist's FeynRules DB entry.

## Important Details
- Working directory: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-331-w67ndnh2/` — contains `TASK.md`, `SM.fr`, `model.fr`, `paper/1611.09337_source.tex`.
- Bash denied except `./frgen` / `./frgen *`; use only file-read/glob/grep/write tools.
- TASK.md rules: no `M$GaugeGroups` (SM add-on); indices `Colour, Gluon, Generation, SU2D, SU2W` from SM.fr; other indices need `IndexRange[Index[X]] = NoUnfold[Range[n]];`; unique labels `S[n]/F[n]/V[n]` with `n >= 100`; `SelfConjugate -> False` for complex, `True` for real; FeynRules syntax values (rationals `-1/3`, decimals `1500.`); every new coupling param gets `InteractionOrder -> {NP, 1}`; free-field kinetic+mass term per new class (`Mass -> {M, value}` symbol); exactly one `LTotal`; no reserved names (Mathematica/FeynRules: `N, C, D, E, I, K, O, HC, CC, FS, DC, del, Eps, Ga, ProjP, ProjM`; SM.fr: `H, Phi, Z, W, A, G, ee, gs, gw, sw, cw, vev, MZ, MW, MD, MS, MT, MH, lam, muH, yu, yd, yl, CKM, u, c, t, d, s, b, e, mu, ta, uq, dq, l, vl, QL, LL`); no primes in `ParticleName` (`+`/`−` acceptable — SM uses `"W+"`/`"e-"`); class indices ≥100; full audit table per term.
- Rule 13: generation couplings must be matrix products (`uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `uqbar.M.uq` — NO explicit `[sp, ff, cc]` indices), not explicit index sums.
- SU(2) conventions: `Phi` Y=+1/2, `LL` Y=−1/2, `QL` Y=+1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`; ProjM = P_L, ProjP = P_R.
- Benchmark **β = Sqrt[3]** ⇒ Q_V=1, Q_Y=2, Q_D=Q_S=−4/3, Q_T=5/3, Q_E=1; a₊=4, a₋=2, b₊=5, b₋=1; renormalizable (no Λ, no CC).
- Feynman-rule ↔ L-coefficient convention: paper vertex g with explicit `i` ⇒ L coeff = g/i (strip i); paper vertex without `i` ⇒ L coeff = g as-is. For VSS form `c·V[mu](S1 del[S2,mu] − S2 del[S1,mu])`, Feynman rule = i·c·(p1−p2)^mu.
- Charge conservation (ΣQ = 0) overrides paper labels where the paper has apparent typos. Resolved field choices already in file: `Yqbar.lbar.El`, `Yqbar.Dqbar.uq`, `Vqbar.uqbar.Tq`, `HY.Elbar.l`, `HVbar.Dqbar.dq`, `HY.Tqbar.dq`, `Yq.Tqbar.dq`.
- **V–W–Y triple gauge (paper 2175)**: paper labels don't conserve charge (−1+1+2=2). Resolution: flip W signs ⇒
  - `V^{-QV} W^- Y^{+QY}` (fields Vqbar, Wbar, Yq) with g = +i e/(√2 sw)
  - `V^{+QV} W^+ Y^{-QY}` (fields Vq, W, Yqbar) with g = −i e/(√2 sw) — Hermitian conjugates.
- **Missing VSS vertices (paper 1762/1772/1782), charge-conserving resolutions**:
  1. `Vq HP HYbar` (paper V+ H− H^{−QY}), L coeff = −e c12 s23/(2 sw)
  2. `W HV HYbar` (paper W+ H^{−QV} H^{−QY}), L coeff = e c23 c13/(√2 sw)
  3. `Yq HVbar HPbar` (paper Y+ H^{−QV} H+), L coeff = −e s12 s13/(√2 sw)
- **Scalar trilinear fix**: current `H2 H0 HP` (ΣQ=+1) and `H3 HV HYbar` (ΣQ=−1) invalid. Replacement set (coefficient `Sqrt[2]*kk*v3`): `H2 H0 H3 + H3 HV HVbar + H2 HV HVbar + H0 HY HYbar + HP HV HYbar + HPbar HVbar HY`. Derivation from f = √2 kk (ε_ijk ρ^i η^j χ^k + h.c.) with VEVs ρ⁰=v1/√2, η⁰=v2/√2, χ⁰=v3/√2 confirmed charge-conserving combos.
- **Neutral quark Yukawa generation structure** (paper 2292–2310): light u (gens 1,2) P12: O21/v2, U21/v2 (h, skipped—SM), U22/v2, U23/v2; t (gen 3) P3: O11/v1, U11/v1, U12/v1, U13/v1 (follows d-type); light d (gens 1,2) P12: O11/v1, U11/v1, U12/v1, U13/v1; b (gen 3) P3: O21/v2, U22/v2, U23/v2 (follows u-type). Remove stray `O21 yd[3,3]` extra term (~line 887). Coefficient form: `O21/Sqrt[2] yu[ff,ff] vev/v2` etc. = O21·m_u/v2.
- **El Yukawa**: add missing `h El El` term: paper −i U31 ME/v3 ⇒ L coeff −U31 MEl/v3. Keep H0 term real (`O31*MEl/v3`) inside `yuk + HC[yuk]` (only non-vanishing Hermitian choice; imaginary coeff would cancel under HC). Skip h-bar-light-fermion rows (already SM LYukawa).
- **Charged light H+ bar u d (matrix form)**: paper light = −√2 V (c12 m_u/v2 P_L + s12 m_d/v1 P_R); tb = +√2 V_tb (s12 m_t/v1 P_L + c12 m_b/v2 P_R) — swapped angles, opposite sign. Matrix elements: MLHP[i,j] (P_L) = −CKM[i,j] c12 yu[i,i] vev/v2 for i,j≤2; = +CKM[3,3] s12 yu[3,3] vev/v1 for i=j=3. MRHP[i,j] (P_R) = −CKM[i,j] s12 yd[j,j] vev/v1 (light); = +CKM[3,3] c12 yd[3,3] vev/v2 (tb). Written as `HP uqbar.MLHP.ProjM.dq + HP uqbar.MRHP.ProjP.dq`.

- A Y+Y− VSS: paper line 2167 gives g = i a₊ e/2 = 2i e (a₊=4) — consistent with existing code `2*ee`; keep.
- L coeff checks confirmed: Z′ couplings `zpQLe/zpQLu/zpQRu/zpQLd/zpQRd/zpQLD` all match code after g/i conversion; D A coupling = −4/3·ee, T A = +5/3·ee, E A = am·ee/2.
- Other confirmed conventions: projectors P1/P2/P3/P12; Z′ matrices zpQLu/zpQRu/zpQLd/zpQRd/zpQLe/zpQRe/zpQLv/zpQLE/zpQRE; scalar zpQLD/zpQRD/zpQLT/zpQRT; heavy A/Z zD/zT/zE/aE; `vyCoup = -ee/(Sqrt[2]*sw)`; widths auto via `Width -> {WZp, 100.}`; `InteractionOrder -> {NP,1}` on couplings only (dropped from masses/vevs); heavy-fermion EM needs explicit `-4/3*ee A[mu] Dqbar.Ga[mu].Dq` (DC on Dq covers only SU(3)); triple gauge A VV = I·a₋·ee/2, A YY = I·a₊·ee/2, Z VV = −I·ee(1+a₋sw²)/(2cw sw), Z YY = I·ee(1−a₊sw²)/(2cw sw), Z′ VV/Z′ YY = −I·Sqrt[3]·ee·a₀/(2cw sw); VVS form `c·V1[mu]V2[mu]S`; LScalarPotential quartics in mass basis + portal `Phibar[ii]Phi[ii]·(H2²/H3²/H0²/HPbar HP)` + f-trilinear; μ² terms omitted (masses in free-field terms).

834: (* ----- Free-field terms: vectors ----- *)
835: LZp := -1/4 FS[Zp, mu, nu] FS[Zp, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZp^2 Zp[mu] Zp[mu];
836: 
837: LVq := -1/2 FS[Vqbar, mu, nu] FS[Vq, mu, nu] + MVq^2 Vqbar[mu] Vq[mu];
838: 
839: LYq := -1/2 FS[Yqbar, mu, nu] FS[Yq, mu, nu] + MYq^2 Yqbar[mu] Yq[mu];

841: (* ----- Free-field terms: real scalars ----- *)
842: LH2 := 1/2 del[H2, mu] del[H2, mu] - 1/2 MH2^2 H2^2;
843: 
844: LH3 := 1/2 del[H3, mu] del[H3, mu] - 1/2 MH3^2 H3^2;
845: 
846: LH0 := 1/2 del[H0, mu] del[H0, mu] - 1/2 MH0^2 H0^2;
847: 
848: (* ----- Free-field terms: complex scalars ----- *)
849: LHP := DC[HPbar, mu] DC[HP, mu] - MHP^2 HPbar HP;
850: 
851: LHV := DC[HVbar, mu] DC[HV, mu] - MHV^2 HVbar HV;
852: 
853: LHY := DC[HYbar, mu] DC[HY, mu] - MHY^2 HYbar HY;

855: (* ----- Free-field terms: Dirac fermions ----- *)
856: LDq := I Dqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Dq, mu] - MDq Dqbar.Dq;
857: 
858: LSq := I Sqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Sq, mu] - MSq Sqbar.Sq;
859: 
860: LTq := I Tqbar.Ga[mu].DC[Tq, mu] - MTq Tqbar.Tq;

862: LEl := Block[{sp, ff},
863:   ExpandIndices[I Elbar[sp, ff].Ga[mu].DC[El[sp, ff], mu] - MEl Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff]]
864: ];

866: (* ----- New Yukawa interactions (paper Table scalar-fermion) ----- *)
867: LYukawaNew := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},
868:   yuk = ExpandIndices[
869:     (* Heavy leptons with neutral scalars (H0, H2, H3) *)
870:     O31*MEl/v3 Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff] H0
871:     - U32*MEl/v3 Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff] H2
872:     - U33*MEl/v3 Elbar[sp, ff].El[sp, ff] H3
873:     (* Heavy quarks D,S,T with chi-like H3 (from y^J qbar chi J) *)
874:     - U33*MDq/v3 Dqbar[sp, cc].Dq[sp, cc] H3
875:     - U33*MSq/v3 Sqbar[sp, cc].Sq[sp, cc] H3
876:     - U33*MTq/v3 Tqbar[sp, cc].Tq[sp, cc] H3
877:     (* H0 with SM fermions (new CP-odd couplings) *)
878:     O21/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] vev/v2 lbar[sp, ff].l[sp, ff] H0
879:     - U22/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] vev/v2 lbar[sp, ff].l[sp, ff] H2
880:     - U23/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] vev/v2 lbar[sp, ff].l[sp, ff] H3
881:     O21/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 uqbar[sp, ff, cc].uq[sp, ff, cc] H0
882:     - U22/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 uqbar[sp, ff, cc].uq[sp, ff, cc] H2
883:     - U23/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 uqbar[sp, ff, cc].uq[sp, ff, cc] H3
884:     O11/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 dqbar[sp, ff, cc].dq[sp, ff, cc] H0
885:     - U12/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 dqbar[sp, ff, cc].dq[sp, ff, cc] H2
886:     - U13/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 dqbar[sp, ff, cc].dq[sp, ff, cc] H3
887:     O21/Sqrt[2] yd[3, 3] vev/v2 dqbar[sp, 3, cc].dq[sp, 3, cc] H0
888:     ,
889:     FlavorExpand -> SU2D
890:   ];
891:   yuk + HC[yuk]
892: ];

894: (* Charged-scalar Yukawa (complex; HC added for h.c.) *)
895: LYukawaCharged := Block[{sp, cc, ff, ff1, ff2, yuk},
896:   yuk = ExpandIndices[
897:     (* H+ bar nu l : sqrt2 ml c12/v2 P_R ; ml = yl vev/sqrt2 *)
898:     c12*vev/v2 yl[ff, ff] HP vlbar[sp, ff].ProjP.l[sp, ff]
899:     (* H^{+QV} bar E nu : -sqrt2 c13 ME/v3 P_L ; charge: HV(+1)+Elbar(-1)+vl(0)=0 *)
900:     - Sqrt[2]*c13*MEl/v3 HV Elbar[sp, ff].ProjM.vl[sp, ff]
901:     (* H^{-QY} bar E l : -sqrt2 (s23 ml/v2 PL + c23 ME/v3 PR) ; HYbar(-2)+Elbar(-1)+l(-1) wait:
902:        use HY(+2)+Elbar(-1)+l(-1)=0 with bilinear bar E l *)
903:     - Sqrt[2]*s23*vev/v2/Sqrt[2] yl[ff, ff] HY Elbar[sp, ff].ProjM.l[sp, ff]
904:     - Sqrt[2]*c23*MEl/v3 HY Elbar[sp, ff].ProjP.l[sp, ff]
905:     (* H+ bar u d : -sqrt2 V (c12 mu/v2 PL + s12 md/v1 PR) *)
906:     - Sqrt[2]*c12/Sqrt[2] yu[ff1, ff1] vev/v2 HP uqbar[sp, ff1, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, ff2, cc] CKM[ff1, ff2]
907:     - Sqrt[2]*s12/Sqrt[2] yd[ff2, ff2] vev/v1 HP uqbar[sp, ff1, cc].ProjP.dq[sp, ff2, cc] CKM[ff1, ff2]
908:     (* H^{-QV} bar D d : -sqrt2 V (c13 MD/v3 PL + s13 md/v1 PR) ; HVbar(-1)+Dqbar(+4/3)+dq(-1/3)=0 *)
909:     - Sqrt[2]*c13*MDq/v3 HVbar Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, ff, cc]
910:     - Sqrt[2]*s13/Sqrt[2] yd[ff, ff] vev/v1 HVbar Dqbar[sp, cc].ProjP.dq[sp, ff, cc]
911:     (* H^{+QY} bar u D : sqrt2 (s23 mu/v2 PL + c23 MD/v3 PR) ; HY(+2)+uqbar(-2/3)+Dq(-4/3)=0 *)
912:     Sqrt[2]*s23/Sqrt[2] yu[ff, ff] vev/v2 HY uqbar[sp, ff, cc].ProjM.Dq[sp, cc]
913:     Sqrt[2]*c23*MDq/v3 HY uqbar[sp, ff, cc].ProjP.Dq[sp, cc]
914:     (* H+ bar t b *)
915:     Sqrt[2]*s12/Sqrt[2] yu[3, 3] vev/v1 HP uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]
916:     Sqrt[2]*c12/Sqrt[2] yd[3, 3] vev/v2 HP uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjP.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]
917:     (* H^{-QV} bar t T : sqrt2 (s13 mt/v1 PL + c13 MT/v3 PR) ; HVbar(-1)+uqbar(-2/3)+Tq(+5/3)=0 *)
918:     Sqrt[2]*s13/Sqrt[2] yu[3, 3] vev/v1 HVbar uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjM.Tq[sp, cc]
919:     Sqrt[2]*c13*MTq/v3 HVbar uqbar[sp, 3, cc].ProjP.Tq[sp, cc]
920:     (* H^{+QY} bar T b : sqrt2 V_tb (c23 MT/v3 PL + s23 mb/v2 PR) ; HY(+2)+Tqbar(-5/3)+dq(-1/3)=0 *)
921:     Sqrt[2]*c23*MTq/v3 HY Tqbar[sp, cc].ProjM.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]
922:     Sqrt[2]*s23/Sqrt[2] yd[3, 3] vev/v2 HY Tqbar[sp, cc].ProjP.dq[sp, 3, cc] CKM[3, 3]
923:     ,
924:     FlavorExpand -> SU2D
925:   ];
926:   yuk + HC[yuk]
927: ];
